You started answering and saying that it was correct, that the SIS in the brigades existed, as far as I understood you, in the units, and that those were, indeed, the tasks which the commanders could issue SIS. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. There was part of a united single SIS within the brigade, and within the brigade the SIS was operating for the needs and requirements of that particular brigade. Therefore, that is the united, single SIS system that existed within the HVO, and now we see it working at the level of the brigade, doing its job in the field of the brigade's remit, which is quite normal. And then once it has carried out its assignments, it will inform the superior SIS officers, right up to the level of the SIS Administration, because he is duty-bound to do that. So he'll do the work for the brigade, and then he will inform the brigade and his superiors up his vertical line, which is the SIS Administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Petkovic, will the assistant commander for SIS in the brigade inform the assistant commander of SIS in the operative zone?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they had the duty to inform him, but directly to send the SIS Centre information first, or the SIS Administration, perhaps, too, and first. So within the SIS system, they were duty-bound to inform the SIS Administration. That's what it says in their rules and regulations, the rules and regulations of the Security and Information Service, which we have looked at in this courtroom and discussed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, the orders for their work, as we have seen on the basis of the one we looked at, did they receive it from the commander under whose command they were, and do they report to him about their work?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are given their assignment both to the commander and the superior level. That's what it says in the regulations, and they are duty-bound to adhere to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. May we have shorter answers, please. And look at P3614 next, please. P3614 is the number, yes. It's a request from you, dated the 21st of July, and what you're requesting is that in view of the situation in the area of responsibility of the 2nd HVO Brigade, you are sending this request to Mr. Lasic to send reports of commanders which are of interest to the commanders of the 2nd Brigade. And then it says: "NS, the Intelligence and SIS section." So you asked for reports from all these individuals linked to certain events; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Madam, I asked for a complete report into everybody, including the commander, including the intelligence personnel and SIS, and some people knew, some people did not, about what was happening in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we now look at 2D3025 next, please. This is an order from Commander Marijan Bradara, brigade command, and it is the Josip Jelacic Brigade, and he is issuing an order to the chief of SIS Brigade and the chief of the 3rd Battalion of Kresevo. And this is what he says, establish the facts straight away, and the reason why the defence line was not taken up. In item 3, it says that persons who fail or obstruct the implementation of the order should be sanctioned. 2D35 -- 2D3025 is the document number. I think I've read it out correctly. 2D3025 is the document I'd like to have us look at next. Have you found it, Mr. Petkovic? You have.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm looking at.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, if we look at number 4, it says that the command of the 3rd Battalion, the Kresevo Battalion, he draws their attention to cases of this kind, and the commander is asking, under item 5, that the persons this order is addressed to shall be held personally responsible "to me." Now, with this type of command or order, issued by the brigade commander to the chief of SIS and chief of the SIS within the 3rd Battalion, are those the tasks and assignments that come within their remit?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the brigade commander can't issue an order to the chief of SIS Administration. All he can do is to issue orders to those in his brigade, and those are the SIS organs working in that particular brigade. But that does not mean that this is some third type of SIS. It's just one single SIS, this one installed in the brigade and working for the requirements of the brigade and battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely why I'm asking you this, Mr. Petkovic, to see what SIS does. That's why I'm asking you. And we'll take a look at another document -- or, rather, two documents. Look at P6791 next, please. This is your order, dated the 22nd of November, 1993, and you speak about the increase of crime, which upsets military discipline. And you demand that an analysis of the crimes committed be undertaken. And under 4, you say: "To engage the SIS organs to deal with these tasks and give them priority." And you refer to Tomislavgrad, Vitez, and so on, and those military districts. Is that correct, it's addressed to Tomislavgrad, Mostar, and Vitez?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So you are addressing them to make things clear, and they are going to involve their assistants, each in his own unit; right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As this deals with crimes in a broad area, they're going to involve their own assistants, the SIS Centre's and sub-centres in their area, so they're going to mobilise the entire SIS apparatus in the region. It does not exclude the involvement of the SIS Centre or asking assistance from the SIS Centre, because you know that in a brigade you only have so many SIS workers.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now, when it comes to reporting, let's look at the next document, which is 4D977. This a report addressed to the Main Staff from Kiseljak. The date is the 7th of June, and the assistant chief for the SIS Brigade, Zeljko Bosnjak, directly informs the Main Staff -- I'm sure you're familiar with this document, as it's a 4D document. And in connection to the letter from the Main Staff, that because of combat in the Kiseljak area, it wouldn't be opportune to discuss the problem of crime at that moment. And then he goes on to say that this will be done when the situation on the ground changes. Right? This document shows that you, in the Main Staff, receive reports from the SIS in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The gentleman is saying that my order to undertake certain action should not be done at the present time, but should be deferred until later. Now, whether he's going to report back to me or not is another question. The order came from me -- or, rather, the Main Staff for them to carry out certain actions to prevent crime. Now, the SIS that was supposed to be in charge of that is writing back to me and saying that it would be a better thing to defer that until later. Now, we should look at his report to see what was actually done. Obviously, a report is due to the commander or chief of the Main Staff from the unit commander who would surely have his SIS operational officer make the report for him.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Petkovic, would you now look at the next document -- or, rather, before we go on to our next document, let's see how orders are issued, when it came to the Medical Corps, SIS, IPD, and so on. And it was a question that Judge Antonetti asked. All I'm going to ask you now is whether what you have just said -- what you have just told us about SIS, that is to say, that the orders by the assistant commanders are received in the same way both for IPD and Logistics and for the Medical Corps, from the commander within their composition --

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same system that applies to the whole of the HVO, from top to bottom. A single system was established both for the Medical Corps, Logistics, and -- what was the other thing you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Petkovic, I asked you whether the assistants for IPD, for the medical corps and for logistics also receive orders from the unit commander they belong to, for their regular duties?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely correct. They will receive orders from their assistants, but it doesn't mean that they will not contact with their superior officers and that they are duty-bound to inform the IPD service or whatever up his vertical line; whether it be SIS, IPD, or -- what was the thing you mentioned? Logistics, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Petkovic, in the operative zone -- or, rather, we have established that there is an assistant for SIS, IPD, Health, and Logistics in the operative zone; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, these assistants, assistants to the commander of the operative zone, for their work, did they report to the commander of the operative zone about their work?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they had to do that, because they were his assistants, so they had to report back to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, the commander of the operative zone, was he duty-bound to send reports to the Main Staff which would be relevant and important to the planning of certain operations or to be able to assess the situation in a certain area on questions of security, morale, logistics, and so on?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely right. The commander must inform the Main Staff on all issues, and this would include the morale of the troops, logistics, and the problems that he might have with the Medical Corps. But he will simultaneously inform the highest levels of Logistics, SIS, IPD, and so on, because future work will depend on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Petkovic, I can't refrain from asking you why it would depend on them.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam counsel, because it is the roof, the upper-most organisation, the blanket organisation in the Ministry of Defence, and they don't just hold press conferences. They are there as the umbrella to explain the policies of Herceg-Bosna and to provide guide-lines and instructions about how the organs -- their organs will be working in the lower units, because somebody has to give guide-lines and instructions. And the commander has responsibility at a lower level, lower than the top man in the Defence Department and later the Ministry of Defence. So that was their task. They have to be in contact with all the forces right down to the lower level, which is a battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you, Mr. Petkovic. And Mr. Bandic, who testified here, agreed with you, too, and he explained that it was the role of the administration to provide professional advice along the lines of what you've just told us. Let's now go on to 4D1700.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just add, when you're talking about Mr. Bandic, Mr. Bandic was in an advisory capacity, but he was also an operative, because operative centres or sub-centres of SIS belonged to him and he led them as an operative.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Petkovic, thank you. We'll soon get to Mr. Bandic. Let's just have a look at two or three documents, orders that Judge Antonetti asked about. Have a look at 4D1700. Have you found it? I assume so. Judge Antonetti asked questions about it yesterday. Please have a look at page 12 in the Croatian version, page 13 in the English version. In this order, signed by Mr. Blaskic, you said it was from March 1993. It says in item 8(a), (b), (c), it says that orders are being issued concerning IPD and SIS issues. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Those are the bodies that exist at those levels, and that is the way in which they have to function. And those bodies, those organs, will have to show the success they've had in those operative zones to their highest organs, because the IPD at the level of defence has to know what's going on down below. So they will go into the field to work, these bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm showing these orders to you. I know it's logical, General Petkovic, but Judge Antonetti asked you whether, in the course of Praljak's questions, whether it meant that the assistant commander had to ask for instructions when issuing certain orders, or could he receive such orders directly from his commander? That's the only reason for which I'm putting this question to you. Let's have a look at 4D475, which deals with the same subject. Let's have a look at item 7 in the document. It's on page 8. That's where we'll start. Item 7 in the English version is on page 7. Similarly, this is an order that is being sent to the IPD. It's an order that's replete for active defence, dated the 23rd of February, 1993. It's an order issued to the IPD. In item 7, item 7(3), an order is issued to security. And then the last bullet says: "SIS offices, as professional organs of the command, directly participate in the organisation and the implementation of security measures in their unit, and they provide assistance for other members of the armed forces." Isn't that what it says, Mr. Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. SIS workers have to assist all those below them. SIS in the operative zone will provide assistance for the SIS lower down, and the [indiscernible] organisation, at its meetings, must prepare all SIS officials, workers for the armed forces. The IPD also has its plans where it prepares its men at lower levels with regard to how to act and under what conditions. We had seen work plans for the IPD, that they should visit units, they should prepare their employees. They don't have to prepare instructions and orders every day. They'll prepare them, they'll provide them with instructions, they will give them guide-lines and tell them what is essential for them to do in their work down there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Petkovic, that wasn't my question. You have repeated that, and you keep repeating that on numerous occasions. I'm showing you documents that show that with regard to orders for defence -- with regard to any orders, the commander who issues the order simultaneously is assigning tasks in that order to his subordinate assistants for SIS and IPD, to assistants for logistics. Am I correct, does this order show that?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those are his assistants, they are his assistants, and he issues orders to them. He probably asked for his assistants to be prepared by people who are more professional than his own people. With regard to such an operation and such a command, well, it's necessary for the highest-level organs to be included. They know a lot more than the others. And then the commander will deal with matters in the field. Whether an area of 70 kilometres is concerned isn't just a matter for the commander of an operative zone.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's have a look at P4778. It's an order dated the 3rd of September, 1993. And, similarly, item 10 says: "Motivate each and every soldier to the maximum." It gives orders for logistics, and this order also contains an order for the Medical Corps. So it has to do with logistical support and obtaining two medical vehicles. Did Commander Siljeg, in this order dated the 3rd of September, include tasks that should be carried out by assistants for IPD and by the assistant for the Medical Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Colonel Siljeg knew what the situation was in his brigade, particularly if this has to do with Rama or Livno. He knows how the Medical Corps functions. He's aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Petkovic, since you said that when such operations are involved, these assistants will certainly ask for assistance from the administrations of the SIS and the IPD -- I'll go back to an order that I have already shown to you. It's your order, the number of which is P6791. It's an order that relates to dealing with criminal activity. The following document, this is your document, but let's see where the SIS assistants went, after your order, to consult. It's document P6822. I believe it should be visible in the e-court system, P6822. Have a look at that. On the basis of this order of yours, Mr. Lasic refers to your order, in fact, and he says that there has been an increase in crime which affects one's reputation. And he says, Send in SIS officials of the first subordinated units to a meeting that will be held with the command of the Mostar Military District. It was sent to Sector North, Sector South, to the Mostar Defence Sector. So can you see that Mr. Lasic, when carrying out his order, sends SIS assistants to a meeting in the Mostar Military District; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were sent to the Mostar Military District, but we don't know whether he found a professional person from the SIS who would prepare his workers. This was just an invitation to a meeting. It would be logical for someone in the Centre for SIS in Mostar to go to the meeting and prepare all the workers from subordinate units for the tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Petkovic, I apologise, I have just one more document to deal with, so I have to hurry. Does this document say that the invitation is addressed to the SIS Administration too? Just tell me that.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't, but we don't know how preparations were made.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So you are making calculations, then?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The speakers are kindly asked to slow down and not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm just talking about professional preparations, and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's just have a look at another document that has to do with Mr. Bandic. It is a document which is an order of yours. You're probably familiar with it. We'll see it in the e-court system, but let's conclude with this. It's document P6137. It's the order that has to do with Stupni Do. It's an order that you issued.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just have a look.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: P6137. It's in e-court system. I just have two questions about this order. Mr. Petkovic, is this order against an unidentified perpetrator, in fact? When you issued the order, was the perpetrator's identity known?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's why we were looking for the perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to the question, Your Honour, but I don't have time to go into that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague will have time in her re-examination, the course of her re-examination. I'd like to remind the Trial Chamber of this.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I assume you're familiar with this. In the course of your testimony, you said that you drafted this order together with Mr. Ivan Bandic. Mr. Ivan Bandic was heard in this court on the 17th of March, 2009. And on page 38094, line 21, I showed this order to Mr. Bandic. And on page 38095, line 1, he answered my question and said that he had never seen this order prior to coming to testify here. Mr. Petkovic, when Mr. Bandic was examined, your Defence team had the opportunity of cross-examining him on two occasions. I have just one question. Did your Defence team show Mr. Bandic -- demonstrate to Mr. Bandic that he was not telling the truth, because he said that it was the first time he had seen -- the first time he saw the order was when he came to testify here? Do you remember whether you contested this claim of his or not? Just tell me that.

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any such statement made by him, but I know that he advised me as to how to phrase certain questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we failed to put certain questions to him. A question obviously failed to challenge that part of his testimony, because there's a significance difference between saying that it's the first time that he saw this and between what you said in the course of your testimony, but I have no more time. Thank you very much, Witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll stop there, because the Tolimir case will be starting in the afternoon. Thank you, and we will resume on Monday at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 1st day of March, 2010, at 2.15 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
